item.title: Ba end seven-year wait with 6-0 victory to reclaim league title
item.description: Dayal's Sawmillers Ba FC have ended a seven-year wait for the national league title after a dominant 6-0 victory over Tailevu Naitasiri FC at the 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba. The victory secured the 2026 Extra Premier League title for the Men in Black and gave the club its record 22nd national league championship.
item.content:encoded:
Dayal's Sawmillers Ba FC have ended a seven-year wait for the national league title after a dominant 6-0 victory over Tailevu Naitasiri FC at the 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

The victory secured the 2026 Extra Premier League title for the Men in Black and gave the club its record 22nd national league championship.

Ba went into the Round 17 match knowing a win would be enough to seal the title and delivered in front of their home supporters.

The hosts were made to work for the breakthrough, with John Orobulu finally finding the back of the net in the 37th minute to give Ba a 1-0 lead at halftime.

Ba stepped up the pressure after the break, scoring five more goals to complete a convincing victory.

Orobulu scored a hat-trick, while Praneel Dayal, Vilitati Kautoga and Shazil Ali also found the net.

The win takes Ba to 39 points, putting the championship beyond the reach of their nearest challengers.

Ba have also secured the title with one match still in hand against defending champions Rewa FC.

The achievement completes a domestic double for Ba, who also won the 2026 BiC Fiji FACT earlier this year.

After seven years of waiting, the Men in Black are once again national league champions and have added a record 22nd title to their history.

item.title: Fiji Pearls need to keep lifting performance ahead of World Cup Oceania Qualifier - Parsons
item.description: Crest Fiji Pearls Coach Michelle Parsons says they have got to keep lifting their perfomance as they prepare for the upcoming World Cup Oceania Qualifier in Tonga next month. Parsons who has just named her squad says that is what they are seeing with these girls, they are so hungry to be better.
item.content:encoded:
Crest Fiji Pearls Coach Michelle Parsons says they have got to keep lifting their perfomance as they prepare for the upcoming World Cup Oceania Qualifier in Tonga next month.

Parsons who has just named her squad says that is what they are seeing with these girls, they are so hungry to be better.

During the recent 2026 Fiji Invitational Tournament, Parsons says she was literally shifting combos to try and make it as hard for them as possible because she needs to see how they respond to either a changing combination or real pressure.

Parsons says there were shifts in combination where she deliberately partnered people up against each other, or with each other, to literally test them as hard as she possibly could.

The World Cup Oceania Qualifiers are from September 14th to 18th.

item.title: Rewa face disappointing 4-1 defeat by Galaxy FC in Champions League opener
item.description: Rewa FC suffered a disappointing 4-1 defeat to Vanuatu's Galaxy FC in their opening match of the OFC Men's Champions League at Churchill Park in Lautoka. Andrew Malakai opened the scoring for Galaxy FC before William Dos Santos Medina added to the lead, while Gabrieli Matanisiga scored Rewa's only goal of the match.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC suffered a disappointing 4-1 defeat to Vanuatu's Galaxy FC in their opening match of the OFC Men's Champions League at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

Andrew Malakai opened the scoring for Galaxy FC before William Dos Santos Medina added to the lead, while Gabrieli Matanisiga scored Rewa's only goal of the match.

Rewa players Gabrieli Matanisiga, Tevita Waranaivalu, Sitiveni Rakai and Merril Nand were all shown yellow cards during the match.

Galaxy FC dominated the second half, with William Dos Santos Medina completing a hat-trick to seal an impressive opening-day victory for the Vanuatu champions.

Meanwhile, in the day's other match, Lae City FC of Papua New Guinea defeated Tupapa Maraerenga of the Cook Islands 4-1 .

Rewa will now face Tupapa Maraerenga at 4pm Wednesday at 4R Stadium Govind Park in Ba.

item.title: Ngshiu family gives back to Lomary Raluve team with timely support
item.description: New Zealand Sevens representative Tone Ngshiu, together with his family and representatives from Nanuku Resort, rallied behind Lomary Secondary School's Under-18 Raluve team by donating training equipment and food supplies during the Vodafone Weet-Bix Raluve National Championship. item.content:encoded:
New Zealand Sevens representative Tone Ngshiu, together with his family and representatives from Nanuku Resort, rallied behind Lomary Secondary School's Under-18 Raluve team by donating training equipment and food supplies during the Vodafone Weet-Bix Raluve National Championship.

The presentation took place following the team's captain's run, with the donations aimed at supporting the players as they prepared for the knockout stages of the competition.

The gifts included training equipment and food items to help the players with their preparations and wellbeing throughout the tournament.

School officials thanked the Ngshiu family and Nanuku Resort for their generosity, saying the gesture lifted the players' spirits and reminded them that they had the support of the wider community.

They say the donation was about more than providing equipment and food—it gave the players confidence and showed them that their commitment and hard work are recognised beyond the rugby field.

The support came before Lomary's quarter-final clash against Bua Central College, with the team going on to defeat Bua Central 38-5 to book a place in the semi-finals.

School officials say acts of generosity such as this inspire young athletes to keep striving for excellence, knowing there are people willing to invest in their future.

item.title: Blue Ray and Tebara Supermarket Salove fight back to draw 1-1 with Savusavu
item.description: Mohammed Feroz , Nilufa Buksh · 09/08/2026 Blue Ray and Tebara Supermarket Meat Salove fought back from a goal down to hold Savusavu to a 1-1 draw in an entertaining Super Premier Division match on the second day of the Matuku Spares Vanua Levu Muslim IDC at Subrail Park.
item.content:encoded:
Mohammed Feroz , Nilufa Buksh · 09/08/2026

Blue Ray and Tebara Supermarket Meat Salove fought back from a goal down to hold Savusavu to a 1-1 draw in an entertaining Super Premier Division match on the second day of the Matuku Spares Vanua Levu Muslim IDC at Subrail Park.

Savusavu made a strong start and took a 1-0 lead into halftime after scoring in the opening spell.

Blue Ray and Tebara Supermarket Salove responded strongly after the break, applying sustained pressure and capitalising on a counter-attack to score the equaliser.

Both teams created chances to snatch the winner, but solid defending and impressive goalkeeping ensured the points were shared.

Speaking to fijivillage Sports after the match, Blue Ray and Tebara Supermarket Salove coach Sabid Ali praised his players for their performance and says the team is now focused on securing a place in the quarter-finals.

Ali says he urged his players to remain disciplined and continue putting pressure on their opponents.

He says his halftime message was simple, to score the equaliser after going into the break trailing by one goal.

Ali also thanked the supporters who travelled from Viti Levu and those who came to Subrail Park to support the tournament.

Meanwhile, defending champions Tasrif Khan Seaqaqa thrashed Korowiri 5-0 in the Super Premier Division, while Batinikama and Basoga played out a goalless draw in the Premier Division.

item.title: Rewa determined to make fans proud in Champions League opener today
item.description: Rewa FC is determined to give 100 percent and make their families and fans proud when they take on Vanuatu’s Galaxy FC in their OFC Men’s Champions League opener at 3pm today. Rewa FC player Setareki Hughes says the team is excited to play the tournament on home soil and has been preparing well for the challenge.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC is determined to give 100 percent and make their families and fans proud when they take on Vanuatu’s Galaxy FC in their OFC Men’s Champions League opener at 3pm today.

Rewa FC player Setareki Hughes says the team is excited to play the tournament on home soil and has been preparing well for the challenge.

Hughes says having eight players from the Pro League, along with players from other Pro League teams, has provided a major boost to the squad.

He says the players are looking forward to giving their best throughout the tournament.

He says Rewa FC expects all teams in their group, including Galaxy FC, Lae City and Tupapa Maraerenga, to provide a tough challenge.

Hughes says the teams have arrived well prepared and expects good matches during the tournament.

Rewa FC will face Galaxy FC at 3pm today at Churchill Park in Lautoka.
